passage: "You came home quiet today, Vikas. Sit, I'll tell you something. I'm Deepak, your Dada, and I was ten once, in Kanpur. A boy named Suraj started calling me Kaalu because my skin was dark. Every day, in front of everyone. It cut me. I began walking the long way to school so I wouldn't pass him. One evening I told my mother, hardly able to get the words out. She held my face and said his words told her about him, not me. Next day she came with me and spoke to my teacher. And there was Bhola, who shared his marbles and never asked why I was sad. So. What happened at school today?"

qa.a: He called him Kaalu, because Deepak's skin was dark.

qa.q: How did the teasing make young Deepak feel, and how can you tell?
qa.a: It hurt him deeply. He said it cut him, and he walked the long way to school to avoid Suraj.

qa.q: What could Vikas do now, and who might help?
qa.a: He can tell a trusted adult such as his Dada what happened and stay close to kind friends. 🤍

qa.q: How might Dada see Vikas coming home quiet?
qa.a: As a sign Vikas is hurting. Dada remembers that feeling, so he shares his own story gently instead of pushing.

grounding: Shows an elder remembering being teased about skin colour, telling a trusted adult, and finding a kind friend.
